pr_body:
This PR fixes hyperflash write issues.
It implements the functionality from mcux-sdk-examples on board evkbimxrt1050:

- [flexspi_hyper_flash_ops.c](https://github.com/nxp-mcuxpresso/mcux-sdk-examples/blob/main/evkbimxrt1050/driver_examples/flexspi/hyper_flash/polling_transfer/flexspi_hyper_flash_ops.c) contains the clock logic.
- [flexspi_hyper_flash_polling_transfer.c](https://github.com/nxp-mcuxpresso/mcux-sdk-examples/blob/main/evkbimxrt1050/driver_examples/flexspi/hyper_flash/polling_transfer/flexspi_hyper_flash_polling_transfer.c) contains the flash_flexspi_hyperflash_lut array.

Fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/53855

One thing to consider is that I notice a difference between your implementation of the clock update sequence versus the SDK's: the SDK calls FLEXSPI_UpdateDllValue() after reconfiguring the clock speed (https://github.com/nxp-mcuxpresso/mcux-sdk-examples/blob/main/evkbimxrt1050/driver_examples/flexspi/hyper_flash/polling_transfer/flexspi_hyper_flash_ops.c#L336). This function does include a 100 NOP delay here: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/hal_nxp/blob/master/mcux/mcux-sdk/drivers/flexspi/fsl_flexspi.c#L466, which could explain why placing a delay before writes from MCUBoot fixes the swap support.

@jeppenodgaard I believe your issue still has to do with code relocation. If you look at the linker file for the MCUX SDK sample, you can see that the SDK relocates the flexSPI and clock drivers to TCM: https://github.com/nxp-mcuxpresso/mcux-sdk-examples/blob/main/evkbimxrt1050/driver_examples/flexspi/hyper_flash/polling_transfer/armgcc/MIMXRT1052xxxxx_flexspi_nor.ld#L89. This is important because the function `CLOCK_GetFreq` call made in `flexspi_clock_get_freq` is *not inline*, and will be in flash unless relocated. I've created a commit that moves the HAL clock driver to ITCM when the flexSPI driver is enabled, which you can see here: https://github.com/nxp-zephyr/hal_nxp/commit/8f5c9b7c9821da65b44860708bea8d0b3633c2b3

With this commit (and the code in this PR) I have been able to get MCUBoot working, both with `tests/boot/test_mcuboot` and the DFU upgrade sample. I've also tested the flash shell (*not the flash_sample shell*) with this PR and `main`, and can confirm the `flash write` command exposes issues with flexSPI driver unless the clocks are reconfigured. It seems that the way the `flash_sample` shell issues writes does not expose this issue.

Given that we are relocating the clock driver to RAM (which will add the `KEEP` flag to all relocated functions), and including new clock configuration code at the SOC level, I'd like to guard this behavior with a Kconfig. Something like `CONFIG_FLASH_MCUX_FLEXSPI_CLOCK_CONFIG`, which when enabled will:
- include SOC-specific clocking functions
- relocate `fsl_clock.c` to RAM in NXP's HAL
- compile in the `memc_flexspi_update_clock` function

On my board, I do not. I just want to make sure that these fixes aren't masking an underlying issue, by introducing a delay where there wasn't one before. One thing the MCUXpresso SDK examples do that our driver does not is disable the SCB cache before performing flexSPI accesses: https://github.com/nxp-mcuxpresso/mcux-sdk-examples/blob/main/evkbimxrt1050/driver_examples/flexspi/hyper_flash/polling_transfer/flexspi_hyper_flash_ops.c#L31

Does calling `SCB_DisableDCache` and `SCB_DisableICache` before erase or writing to the flash (and then calling the associated `SCB_Enable*` functions afterwards) fix your issue, without the more generic clock calculation present in your latest commit?

I added a print before the `return` in `memc_flexspi_update_clock`.

```
div 3, flexspi_clock_get_freq() 65454543, CLOCK_GetClockRootFreq(kCLOCK_FlexspiClkRoot) 65454543
div 0, flexspi_clock_get_freq() 261818172, CLOCK_GetClockRootFreq(kCLOCK_FlexspiClkRoot) 261818172
```

On `bugfix/mimxrt1050_hyperflash_write_2`
```
div 2, flexspi_clock_get_freq() 87272724, CLOCK_GetClockRootFreq(kCLOCK_FlexspiClkRoot) 87272724
div 0, flexspi_clock_get_freq() 261818172, CLOCK_GetClockRootFreq(kCLOCK_FlexspiClkRoot) 261818172
```

The get clock functions return the same value. However the divider is different.

Adding `SCB_DisableDCache(); SCB_DisableICache();` after `irq_lock()` and `SCB_EnableDCache(); SCB_EnableICache();` before `irq_unlock()` does not seem to change anything.

Setting the divider to `2` instead of `3` in `bugfix/mimxrt1050_hyperflash_write` makes it run stable. This does not make much sense to me since the clock then runs faster while writing. Setting the divider to 5 which makes `flexspi_clock_get_freq()` return a value < 50 MHz, which as far as I can tell is the value we are looking for, also make the system crash.

That is strange. I think one thing to try is to move the USB DFU sample to run from RAM, to eliminate any potential read-while-write issues that could stem from executing from flash while writing to it.

I've created a branch here where the `dfu-usb.sh` script is updated to build the USB DFU sample (and hello world sample) for RAM loading with MCUBoot: https://github.com/nxp-zephyr/zephyr/tree/bugfix/mimxrt1050_hyperflash_write_ramload. issue_context.title: mimxrt1050_evk invalid writes to flash
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
Flash write operations to the external hyperflash are most of the time invalid.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
Test with usb dfu sample:
```
BOARD=mimxrt1050_evk && west build -b $BOARD -d build_bl bootloader/mcuboot/boot/zephyr && west build -b $BOARD zephyr/samples/subsys/usb/dfu -d build_dfu -- -DCONFIG_MCUBOOT_SIGNATURE_KEY_FILE=\"bootloader/mcuboot/root-rsa-2048.pem\" -DCONFIG_SHELL=y -DCONFIG_FLASH_SHELL=y -DCONFIG_FLASH_MAP_SHELL=y && west build -b $BOARD zephyr/samples/hello_world -d build_hello_world -- -DCONFIG_BOOTLOADER_MCUBOOT=y '-DCONFIG_MCUBOOT_SIGNATURE_KEY_FILE="bootloader/mcuboot/root-rsa-2048.pem"' && west flash -d build_bl && west flash -d build_dfu && sleep 3 && sudo dfu-util --alt 1 --download build_hello_world/zephyr/zephyr.signed.bin
```
After the transfer write `mcuboot` in the terminal. MCUboot will not be able to read the secondary image.

Test with flash_shell sample:
```
west build -b mimxrt1050_evk zephyr/samples/drivers/flash_shell/ && west flash
```
Write various byte sequences to see errors (see log below).

**Logs and console output**
```
uart:~$ flash read 0x340040 0x40
ff ff ff ff | ff ff ff ff |ff ff ff ff | ff ff ff ff
ff ff ff ff | ff ff ff ff |ff ff ff ff | ff ff ff ff

Reading back written bytes:
12 30 56 78

12 30 56 78 | ff ff ff ff |ff ff ff ff | ff ff ff ff
ff ff ff ff | ff ff ff ff |ff ff ff ff | ff ff ff ff

ff ff ff ff | ff ff ff ff |ff ff ff ff | ff ff ff ff
```
